front: What is the most common valvular problem to monitor after tetralogy of Fallot repair?
back: Chronic pulmonary regurgitation (nearly universal after a transannular RVOT patch). Assessed with PR pressure half-time (< 100 ms → severe), vena contracta width, holodiastolic PA flow reversal, and progressive RV dilation.

front: What ECG finding after TOF repair predicts SCD risk?
back: QRS duration > 180 ms predicts ventricular tachycardia and sudden cardiac death.

front: After atrial switch (Mustard/Senning) for d-TGA, name three important echo findings to look for.
back: 1) Systemic (morphologic) RV dysfunction. 2) Systemic AV (tricuspid) valve regurgitation. 3) Baffle stenosis or leak. Also atrial arrhythmias and sinus node dysfunction.

front: How is a baffle leak diagnosed after an atrial switch operation?
back: Agitated saline contrast injected into an upper extremity vein — bubbles crossing into the systemic (arterial) circulation indicate a leak from the systemic-venous baffle into the pulmonary-venous baffle.

front: After Jatene arterial switch, what specific coronary complication should be screened for?
back: Coronary ostial stenosis at the reimplantation site. Ischemia may manifest as regional wall-motion abnormalities on stress imaging or ventricular arrhythmia.

front: After the Ross operation, what problem may progressively develop over decades?
back: Neo-aortic root dilation and neo-aortic regurgitation — because the pulmonary autograft is now bearing systemic pressures. The pulmonary homograft in the pulmonary position may also degenerate.

front: What is the most common echo finding to screen for after coarctation repair?
back: Recoarctation (persistent or recurrent narrowing at the repair site) and — after patch aortoplasty — aneurysm formation. Also assess for persistent hypertension.

front: Which arrhythmia is expected after ventriculotomy for VSD or TOF repair?
back: Right bundle branch block (from disruption of the right bundle during ventriculotomy). Complete heart block from damage near the AV node may occur near the perimembranous VSD — pacemaker dependent.

front: What are the components of a Fontan pathway assessment on echo?
back: 1) SVC-to-PA anastomosis patency. 2) IVC baffle / extracardiac conduit (look for obstruction, thrombus). 3) Systemic ventricular function. 4) AV valve regurgitation. 5) Fenestration flow direction. 6) Thrombus in the Fontan circuit.
